sanskrit:
संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः।
योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म नचिरेणाधिगच्छति।।
caption:
Kṛṣṇa warns about the difficulty of artificial renunciation. ‘sannyāsas tu mahā-bāho duḥkham āptum ayogataḥ’ (Merely renouncing all activities yet not engaging in the devotional service of the Lord is painful). If you stop working but don’t start serving, you create a vacuum. The mind needs engagement. A vacuum leads to frustration and eventual fall-down. But ‘yoga-yukto munir brahmā na cireṇādhigacchati’ (One engaged in devotional service reaches the Supreme without delay). The yogī is busy serving; he has no time for Māyā. His renunciation is a natural byproduct of his higher taste.
